free_tier.stated: The free edition provides 1 GB of traffic per month; when it runs out you wait for the next month's reset or expand it through official tasks, with no compulsory payment. [translated]

egress.terms: 1 GB per month on the free edition, resettable monthly or expandable through in-product tasks whose size is not stated.; ingress: udp
egress.free_allowance: 1 GB per month on the free edition, resettable monthly or expandable through in-product tasks whose size is not stated.

interface_detail: Windows, Linux and NAS clients; a web console at console.hsk.oray.com manages mappings and domains.
tooling: vendor client on Windows/Linux/NAS plus wg-quick on the local box
chaining: 1 GB/month cannot carry a WG session for long; useful only as a reachability fallback for a control plane.

limits.value: 1 Mbps on the free edition, with a 18:00-08:00 speed boost
real-name verification before the first mapping

binding_note: Either of the other two would fail first in arithmetic (1 GB/month is 0.0009 TiB), but the client never reaches the counter: the real-name gate sits at registration.

identity_cost.detail: Registration requires real-name verification before a mapping can be added: 'register a Peanut Hull account and complete real-name verification (the free edition needs the basic check)'. The checks offered are mainland identity checks.

reliability_note: Free-edition bandwidth is shaped to 1 Mbps outside an 18:00-08:00 window; the vendor rates free-edition stability at 99.5 percent.
confidence_note: Quota, bandwidth, mapping count and the real-name step are all on the vendor's own pages read today. What would raise the rung is a probe of a UDP mapping, which needs a verified account.

evidence.proved: free edition provides 1 GB per month and 1 Mbps, with a night-time speed boost
free edition is 1 Mbps, 2 mapping routes, 10 concurrent connections, 1 free shell domain; protocol may be TCP/UDP or ALL; real-name verification required
the paid ladder starts at CNY 1299/year, so the free edition is the only zero-cost rung

notes: The largest consumer tunnel brand in China and the one an English reader is most likely to have heard of. Two independent blocks: a 1 GB monthly counter and a mainland real-name check. The free external port can be randomised or set by the operator, and the vendor says free users can switch ports to pick a lower-latency node, so port stability is a choice rather than a guarantee.

extras.wg_detail: The mapping form takes a protocol of 'TCP/UDP' or 'ALL', so a public UDP port can be mapped to a local UDP listener, which is all a WG endpoint needs. No WG config is issued.
extras.volume_stated: 1 GB per month on the free edition, resettable monthly or expandable through in-product tasks whose size is not stated.
extras.transit_note: Oray cloud relays every byte; the vendor states the client opens an encrypted tunnel to the cloud and external requests are forwarded inward.
